claims.text: Laser surface alloying with WS2 nanoparticles will reduce both coefficient of friction and wear rate in a high-entropy alloy.
The untreated starting high-entropy alloy contains no self-lubricating phases.
The proposed treatment incorporates approximately 1–2 vol% WS2 nanoparticles into the alloy.
The WS2 nanoparticles will be distributed uniformly within the top approximately 100 µm.
The treatment will remain effective under sliding or rolling contact from room temperature to approximately 600–800 °C.
The treatment can remain effective in controlled environments that may be oxidizing.
Laser treatment will produce a uniform dispersion of WS2 nanoprecipitates in the near-surface region.
WS2 nanoprecipitates will migrate to the contact interface during mechanical sliding.
The interfacial WS2 will form an in situ low-shear-strength lubricious tribofilm.
The tribofilm will lower friction and wear by reducing direct metal-to-metal contact.
The untreated alloy may have a coefficient of friction near 0.6.
The treatment will reduce coefficient of friction by approximately 20–30% relative to the untreated alloy under typical service conditions.
The treatment will reduce wear rate by approximately 20–30% relative to the untreated alloy under typical service conditions.
The untreated alloy will exhibit higher friction and wear than the treated alloy under identical test conditions.
The benefits may diminish at extreme contact pressures or high sliding speeds outside the typical operational envelope.
Nonuniform WS2 distribution caused by processing variation may diminish the beneficial effects.
Failure to achieve at least a 20% reduction in both friction coefficient and wear rate relative to untreated controls is defined as a falsifying outcome.
